correctness.rationale: An isolated selected vertex confines the selected vertices on the opposite side to its unique matched nonneighbor. If that vertex is absent, domination forces the whole original side. If it is present, a forced defender swap against a missing same-side vertex forces a unique omission, and a second attack yields no isolated selected vertex after any defender swap; the no-omission case fails similarly. The two bipartition classes are directly shown secure. Exhaustive definition-level enumeration for n=3 through 7 confirms exactly two sets for n at least four.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete feasible-set classification on a canonical regular bipartite family, not just a parameter value. Its motivation is intrinsic to the invariant: the foundational source says K_{n,n} has no isolate secure dominating set, whereas removing a single perfect matching creates exactly two. This exposes a sharp edge-deletion boundary and shows how unique nonneighbors supply the isolated backup while forcing swap rigidity.
